scope_note: Blender 5.2 LTS manual, one Unreal Engine 4.27 official destruction overview, and Cell Fracture distribution/legacy pages are the verified basis. No Blender or engine run. UE5/Unity/Godot destruction APIs are not asserted.

sources.title: Rigid Body Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Rigid body scope, active/passive bodies, animation interaction, simulation override, scale, mesh-only restriction.
supports: Rigid bodies move/orient objects but do not deform geometry.
Only mesh objects can participate in Blender rigid body simulation.
Active bodies are simulated, passive bodies are animated, and dynamic transforms are overridden by the simulation.
limits: Blender-specific; not an engine destruction API.

sources.title: Rigid Body Collisions
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Primitive/mesh/convex shapes, compound parent, collision source base/deform/final, deforming, friction/bounciness, margin.
supports: Compound parent combines child collision shapes and is usually faster/more stable than an equivalent mesh shape.
Collision source can be base mesh, deformed mesh, or final evaluated mesh; deformation can be enabled.
Primitive centers of gravity are geometric centers, while convex/mesh shapes use object origin.
limits: No universal fragment size, margin, or collision count.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: Rigid Body Constraints Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Constraint host/anchor behavior, breakable threshold, disable collisions, limits, iterations, Child Of alternative, Motor exception.
supports: Constraints usually attach to an Empty; anchor points are computed at start and fixed in each body's local space.
Breakable allows constraint failure at an impulse threshold; Disable Collisions lets constrained bodies pass through each other.
Breakable is disabled for Motor constraints.
If the fixed-anchor model is limiting, the manual suggests multiple objects plus a non-physics Child Of setup.
limits: Constraint break is not mesh fracture; it creates no new surfaces.
No engine export guarantee.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: Rigid Body Tips
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Bake to keyframes, steps per second, solver iterations, small objects, thin mesh tunneling, collision thickness.
supports: Rigid body results can be baked to ordinary keyframes.
Small objects are unstable in the current simulation; the manual suggests about 20 cm as a practical guideline.
Thin mesh shapes can tunnel and may need thickness or collision margin; excessive steps are not a universal fix.
limits: The 20 cm suggestion is a guideline, not a hard domain gate.
Baking transforms is not equivalent to a vertex-animation/VAT pipeline.

sources.title: Rigid Body World
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Rigid Body World collection membership and constraint collection.
supports: Only rigid bodies and constraints in the Rigid Body World collection(s) are taken into account by the simulation.
limits: Does not define engine-side ownership or networking.

sources.title: Motor Constraint
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Motor rotation/translation, axis semantics, Hinge comparison, alignment warning, target velocity/max impulse.
supports: Motor rotation uses the constraint host's X axis; Hinge uses Z.
Misaligned axes can make the motor appear ineffective because the hinge blocks motion.
limits: Blender mechanism only; not a runtime fracture or engine joint contract.

sources.title: Armature Modifier
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Armature deformation purpose, vertex groups/envelopes, multi-modifier mixing.
supports: The Armature modifier deforms existing mesh vertices through vertex groups or envelopes.
It is a deformation path, not a topology-changing fracture path.
limits: Does not define whether an engine can destructively modify the mesh at runtime.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: Skinning Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Object/bone parenting versus Armature modifier; only the modifier changes vertex/control-point relative positions.
supports: Bone-parented objects are transformed as wholes and never deformed.
Only the Armature-modifier path deforms geometry.
limits: Conceptual distinction, not a destruction workflow.

sources.title: Armature Deform Parent
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Armature Deform parenting, Empty/Automatic/Envelope weights, Cube+BoneA/B/C example, overwrite warning.
supports: Armature Deform parenting creates the armature parent relationship and an Armature modifier.
Empty Groups creates empty same-named groups; Automatic Weights can need manual correction.
Automatic/envelope weights overwrite existing same-named vertex group content.
limits: Not a destruction example; no fracture, mass, collision, or engine import.

sources.title: Pose Apply
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Pose as Rest Pose and Visual Transform to Pose.
supports: Pose as Rest Pose permanently changes the armature rest state and may require re-binding and animation/constraint/driver adjustment.
Visual Transform to Pose bakes evaluated constraint results into regular pose transforms.
limits: Not run; no destruction asset was bound or baked.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: glTF 2.0
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Supported features, animation modes, object/pose-bone/shape-key limits, sampling, armature export options.
supports: glTF animation covers object transforms, pose bones, and shape keys; physics/material property animation is outside the supported set.
Actions must be active or stashed to NLA and sampling is recommended when constraints are involved.
The read Blender glTF documentation describes mesh/skin/animation, not a destruction asset container; extensions and custom consumers were not assessed.
limits: Does not define engine-side fracture, chunk ownership, or cache formats.

sources.title: FBX (Legacy)
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Constraint omission, baking, bone orientation correction, armature instance limitation.
supports: FBX writes constraint results as keyframes but does not save constraints.
Bone orientation may require correction after import; armature instances are not supported.
limits: Not an engine destruction asset format.

sources.title: Chaos Destruction Overview
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Full overview: Geometry Collections, fracture methods/sub-fracture, levels, clustering, max cluster level, damage thresholds, cluster group index, collision particles fraction, fields and anchors.
supports: Geometry Collections, fracturing, clustering, connection graph, and fields form a destruction asset/system separate from skinning.
Small modules versus larger combined modules trade placement flexibility against draw calls, seams, and repetition.
Fracture levels and clustering can control visual detail and rigid-body counts; Max Cluster Level limits breakage depth.
Damage thresholds are authored per level/actor; the example uses descending thresholds, but values are illustrative.
DynamicState can switch states (Sleeping/Kinematic/Static/Dynamic/User Defined); Kill and Anchor fields handle cleanup and support locking.
Collision Particles Fraction affects collision quality; low values can cause incorrect collision.
limits: Only UE 4.27; do not infer UE5 field names, defaults, behavior, or performance.
No engine run, threshold calibration, visual check, or network test.
Example values are not universal defaults.

sources.title: Cell Fracture — Blender Extensions
sources.author: Blender Extensions / original authors ideasman42, phymec, Sergey Sharybin
sources.read_scope: Extension listing: bundled in Blender 4.1, current limited-support extension, location, authors, compatibility.
supports: Cell Fracture was bundled in Blender 4.1 and is now an extension with limited support.
The extension lists Blender 4.2 and newer compatibility.
It is not evidence that Blender 5.2.1 has it installed.
limits: Listing metadata only; no code or operation was executed.
Current extension behavior and bugs were not tested.

sources.title: Cell Fracture — Blender 3.5 Manual
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Historical activation/usage: object mode, operator search, settings, next-layer output, bundled GPL add-on.
supports: The historical workflow selects an object, runs 'Cell fracture selected mesh', configures settings, and places fragments on the next layer.
Cell Fracture was bundled at Blender 3.5.
limits: Blender 3.5 is old; not evidence of Blender 5.2.1 behavior or current operator/API.
Page is marked Todo and refers to archived old docs.

sources.title: object_fracture_cell repository README
sources.author: Dustin-Conlon / Cell Fracture community
sources.read_scope: README: formerly bundled through Blender 4.1, now an Extensions-platform add-on, community-maintained, no support expected, build command.
supports: Cell Fracture is community-maintained as an extension and is no longer a guaranteed built-in.
The project explicitly says no support is expected.
limits: README only; source code internals were not read, and the build command was not run.
No license or version compatibility was independently verified beyond the listing.

sources.title: Add-ons — Blender 5.2 LTS Manual
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Add-ons index listing (Node Wrangler, Rigify, glTF 2.0, UI Translations, VR Scene Inspection).
supports: The Blender 5.2 manual add-ons index does not list Cell Fracture.
limits: An index absence is not proof of the local installation state; it only shows the official manual scope. The local add-on state was not run.

sources.title: Weight Paint Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Normalized weight workflow and Armature auto-normalization.
supports: Deformation weights are normally normalized; the Armature modifier normalizes automatically.
Weight locking and auto-normalize help redistribute weights.
limits: Does not imply a universal four-influence limit or validate auto weights.

sources.title: Parenting Objects
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Object parenting, Keep Transform/Parent Inverse, Clear Parent, non-uniform scale limitation.
supports: Object parent transforms children; Keep Transform preserves world placement via Parent Inverse.
Non-uniform parent scale with rotation can cause shear that may be lost when clearing parent.
limits: Does not define engine attachment/ownership behavior.
